utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. The Prosecutor versus Dragan Kolundzija, case number IT-95-8-PT.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, my name is Niemann, and I appear with my colleague Mr. Keegan, and Ms. Reynders is the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Where is Mr. Vucicevic? Mr. Niemann, do you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I haven't heard from Mr. Vucicevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you know if he's in the building?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand that Ms. Reynders made an enquiry in the Bel Air Hotel, and she did discover that they had checked in there. But whether he's in the building or not, I don't know, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It may be that he's in the Defence counsel room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm getting signals from the Defence counsel in a related case outside that he's apparently here and is in the back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's apparently on his way. We'll wait for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. I sincerely apologise for not having my robes on, but I was under the impression that this hearing was to commence at 2.30, according to your previous orders while I was here before you the last time. If you would grant me a privilege to appear to expedite these proceedings as it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We shall, and we'll be going on with the further appearance in order for your client to plead to the additional counts.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, there is kind of a housekeeping matter here that the panel has to make a decision, because I have come from Prijedor. The wife of the accused and his two children, 14 and 15, are in the lobby, and they would like to be present in the visitors' gallery. The passes have been issued. However, for the children, the decision of the Chamber is needed so they could be present here. What I have received -- information I have received, depending on the type of the matters that are going to be discussed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, very well. We shall give the children leave to attend. Now, Mr. Vucicevic, as far as the amended indictment is concerned, I take it that the accused has had a copy of the indictment in a language which he understands, that you've had the chance of going through it with him, and he understands it insofar as he can.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have been on a field trip in Prijedor over the last ten days, and I am not aware that the amended -- the last submission that I have tendered to the panel was objection to the indictment, to the amendment of the indictment. I do not know whether or not you ruled on the amendment. As such, I haven't had an opportunity to review it with my client, so I could not advise him on this matter. I do sincerely apologise, but I have no knowledge of this. If I may continue --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You must have known. Just a moment. You must have known for a long time that it was likely that he would be called upon to plead to these matters. The further appearance was ordered some time ago. Now, is he in a position to plead or not to plead to these counts?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I cannot advise him, you know, how to plead. I can, in general, tell him -- I have talked to him. He is in a position to plead not guilty, and that is, you know, his decision and my advice to him from the very beginning. But I think considering the fairness of the proceedings, which is of the utmost, you know, concern to you, Sir, it behooves me to state the fact that I'm unaware of when the amendment has been confirmed and whether it was confirmed by a Confirming Judge or this Trial Chamber. I have no notice of that, you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Give me the dates, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may add further --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. We've heard enough for the moment. It's a matter we want to consider.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may help you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. We are conferring.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, could you help me with the dates? The dates that we have recorded is that the indictment was confirmed, as amended, on the 30th of August; it was issued on the 9th of September. I'm told it was faxed to Defence counsel that day, and there was an order for this appearance on the 17th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That's right, yes. Those dates are right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Mr. Niemann. Mr. Vucicevic, since you have not conferred on this matter with your client, it's not fair on him to ask him to plead to the indictment. Obviously, he should have the opportunity of your advice. But that said, you should have done this before. In our judgement, you had plenty of time in which to confer with your client and be ready for this appearance. We will put the matter back until the 11th of October at 9.30, by which time we shall expect Mr. Kolundzija to be in a position to plead, having gone through the indictment, your having gone through it with him. Now, that brings us to another matter which concerns your absence yesterday. This is not a matter which we take lightly. The fact was this, that this case was listed with another case. Everybody was here, including the four accused in that case and their counsel. Everybody was ready to deal with hearings, one of which was the joinder application which affected your client. The result of your absence was that that hearing was in jeopardy. We had to consider whether we could go ahead with it or not. In fact, we decided to do so, having had written submissions by yourself. But the upshot was that your client was left unrepresented in this court, grave inconvenience was caused, at the least, and not a word from yourself, let alone your sending a substitute or appearing. Now, these all are serious matters, because it's a professional obligation for counsel to appear in court in which he's instructed at the time which he is to do so. We have in mind to issue you with a formal warning about this sort of conduct, ignoring the orders of the Court and therefore being liable to obstruct the proceedings, the proper conduct of the proceedings, and we have in mind to draw these matters to the attention of the Registrar, for her to take what action she thinks fit. We shall hear you, of course, before we take that action, but would you bear in mind that we have already taken up some time in this abortive hearing. Now, what do you want to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, even though you and me and the Honourable Judge from Jamaica are educated in the Anglo-Saxon law, my father was a lawyer in the former Yugoslavia, and in growing up he had told me one thing that I would forever keep in mind, and that is, "Audiatur et altera pars." I am deeply hurt by the words that Honourable Judge May has uttered now. However --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Vucicevic, we do not want to know about your feelings. What we wish to hear is any --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: You will hear the facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Listen. We want to hear any explanation which you have as to why you weren't here yesterday and why we should not report you to the Registrar. Now, if there is anything you want to say about that, now is your opportunity. We're giving you the opportunity, but limit it to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: I have not received a notice, either actual or constructive, of the hearing that had happened yesterday, number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll hear -- I have made enquires about this, and we'll hear from the Registrar as to what happened, as to whether any notice was sent or not. I want to hear what the position is.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Registry has faxed the scheduling order on the 20th of September to Mr. Vucicevic, his fax number, and the amended indictment has also been faxed to the counsel on the 9th of September, to his fax number so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Vucicevic, you've heard what the Registry has said about this matter, that it was sent to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: According to the practices of the Registry, the counsel travelling to the field is provided with the airfare and other travelling arrangements by the Registry. I departed Chicago on September 15th, I was at the seat of the Tribunal on September 16th, and from there on, I was in Prijedor. I do not know where that notice went, but when I'm in Chicago, I do have difficulties communicating with Bosnia. The connections from the United States cannot be obtained by telephone to Belgrade, and there is a selective possibility to talk to certain people. Even when I was in Kovacevic's case, I could not get his home, I couldn't get some of his relatives, I couldn't get some of the witnesses, and now again I cannot get Kolundzija's family. I do not want that, but when I ring the phone, basically, it doesn't sound busy; it just sounds some different sound. So nobody from Chicago could get hold of me, in case it was faxed to my office in Chicago where there was nobody available at that time, and I was on a field trip. The Registry had known exactly where I was. A simple inquiry or a simple telephone call from here to Prijedor, either to the police or somebody in city hall or to the SFOR, international police force in town, could have located me. Your Honour, I am doing my best to investigate the case, to become available, to use the scanty communication lines that are available, but whatever I have done, sometimes the people who are informing, it's just not -- this job is not done unless somebody is notified. Putting the paper and sending it through the fax doesn't mean that I do know. That's what I would like to convey to you, Your Honour, because I hold this Court in a high regard. I respect my client, just as so many Muslim prisoners that are in the United States whom I interviewed who think that if it wasn't for him, there would have been so many more victims on that night that is basically -- the basis of his indictment. Your Honour, if anything, I would have wanted, because that was an interest of my client and also a service of our profession, and with a high regard to this Court, I would have been here had I known it. Your Honour, I can't help --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let me interrupt to find out this: Was the fax received, is there any information as to that, in Chicago?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know that, Your Honour. There was nobody in the office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm asking the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We have a confirmation, an okay fax, and that means that the fax has been received to the place where it's sent to. As far as I know, it has been sent to your office in the United States, which is the office and the number that you gave the Registry to have your materials received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Vucicevic, if you're away from the office, you have an obligation to be in touch to see if orders of this sort are sent out, and it's no excuse to say, "Well, I was out of the office and therefore I didn't receive the notification."

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that would be the case if I had been vacationing or not pursuing the business of this Tribunal on the explicit travel arrangements provided by the Registry. The Registry knew my whereabouts. This is a short-notice order, and if they wanted me noticed -- and if they wanted to really carry this out diligently, they could have found me there. Your Honour, let me just be as candid as possible. I couldn't talk to my wife for the time that I was in Chicago either because communications -- there is something. It is ten dollars a minute to call from Bosnia. The people that I was staying with, considering all the economics of the scale, that would be too much, and I do not want to finance anybody who is tied up with the case and is extending me hospitality. Your Honour, this was a very sensitive matter, and I'm sorry that that happened, although I feel no personal fault at this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: May I just continue with something else?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. Unless you've got something relevant to say, we've got another case to hear, Mr. Vucicevic. Now, unless there's something else relevant you want to say, we can't deal with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, relevant to the confirmation of the indictment, on September 9th, I have received the same copy of the indictment without any decision of the Court. I did not know whether that was a copy of the indictment that was either rejected by this Chamber, that was confirmed by this Chamber, or whether that was, you know, sent to the Confirming Judge. I did not receive a decision of this Court on the 9th. When I came, I was hoping that something is going to be in my locker, that usually is, that copies are being sent to the counsel's locker. I hadn't found the decision in my locker either at that time. As I was in a hurry to proceed, I proceeded to -- because in my submissions to you, there was quite a bit of indecision on the part of the Prosecution whether the proposed amendment is still before the Confirming Judge, is it before you? I considered that an attempt -- in my mind, I considered that an attempt of the Prosecutor to secure perhaps an amended indictment before the Confirming Judge should you, as the panel, decline to decide, and I haven't read the decision. I do have -- since I have -- if you give us half an hour or 15 minutes, I could confer with my client, I could advise him, and he would be ready to plead, because we had gone over that proposed indictment. The only thing that I'm unaware of, I'm unaware of who confirmed the indictment, and if I read a decision of such a body, if it's yours, I'm happy to accommodate the schedule. But, Your Honours, that would be a little bit because I'm flying from Chicago to here, and kindly, since I've already spent 10 days, and by the time I leave here, it will be 15 days in Europe, to come back on short notice, it is going to be a difficulty. I think we can finish this matter -- it would be absolutely possible if you give us a recess of 15 minutes, we could come back and plead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Vucicevic, we will accommodate your difficulties to this extent: that the matter will be dealt with at 2.30 tomorrow, but you must understand that by doing so, you affect other cases, other counsel, other accused whose cases can't be heard while we'll dealing with matters which, in our view, you should have dealt with to allow us to go ahead with this hearing today. Now, these are, as I've said, all serious matters. We hear your explanation. We've heard that these documents have been sent to your professional address. We are not satisfied with the state of affairs at all. We shall report the matter to the Registrar, it's then a matter for her what action she takes, and also issue a warning under Rule 46(A) to yourself due to your absence from the hearing yesterday. We will adjourn this until half past two tomorrow when we shall expect your client to be in the position to plead to this indictment. Very well. Half past two tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Appearance adjourned at 2.50 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 29th day of September, 1999, at 2.30 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
